newsitem.title: CANADA: TENNIS-SANCHEZ VICARIO, PIERCE UPSET IN CANADIAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SANCHEZ VICARIO, PIERCE UPSET IN CANADIAN OPEN.

text.p: Fifth-seeded Arantxa Sanchez Vicario of Spain and sixth-seeded Mary Pierce of France were upset in third-round matches Thursday at the $926,250 Canadian Open.
Sanchez Vicario, ranked 11th in the world, was beaten by 10th-seeded American Mary Joe Fernandez 6-4 6-3 and the 10th-ranked Pierce lost to qualifier Rita Grande of Italy 6-2 6-2.
With top-seeded Monica Seles getting a day off, the highest seeded players in action were third seed Amanda Coetzer of South Africa and fourth seed Lindsay Davenport of the United States.
Coetzer, ranked sixth, beat 11th-seeded Kimberly Po 6-4 6-3 and the fifth-ranked Davenport downed 49th-ranked Magui Serna of Spain 7-5 6-4.

Also advancing to Friday's quarter-finals were seventh-seeded Conchita Martinez of Spain, a 6-1 6-4 winner over Yayuk Basuki of Indonesia, and eighth-seeded Anke Huber of Germany, a 6-3 6-4 winner Sandrine Testud of France. Unseeded Magdalena Maleeva of Bulgaria, ranked 43rd, defeated Naoko Sawamatsu of Japan 7-5 6-4.

Pierce never was in the 67-minute match with Grande, who scored her first win over a top-10 player. "I basically had a pretty bad day at the office," Pierce said, "but I have to give Rita credit, she played well.
"I was really impatient and I think I need to find ways during matches like this to find solutions. I need another way to win a match if what normally works for me isn't working."
Grande, a 22-year-old ranked 69th, said: "I don't think she played so good because she played on Tuesday and then had a day off. But I served well and played my best tennis."

Grande, who lost to Seles 6-3 6-1 in the second round in Palo Alto, California, three weeks ago, will meet the world number three in the quarter-finals. "Seles is such a good player and she just played too fast tennis for me," Grande said. "I think I just have to go play and enjoy."
Fernandez, 25, defeated Sanchez Vicario, her doubles partner this week, for only the fourth time in 11 matches.

"I tried to attack the short ball and come in and not get into long rallies with her because you end up over-hitting because she gets everything back," Fernandez said. "It was important for me to take chances."
"She attacked the ball well today," Sanchez Vicario said, "plus I hit some unforced errors that I don't normally make. That was the difference."
Fernandez next plays Maleeva. She holds a 2-1 career edge over the 22-year-old Bulgarian.
Davenport must overcome a more difficult history in her quarter-final against Martinez. The 25-year-old Spaniard leads 5-1 in their head-to-head meetings, winning the last five.
"I don't have a good record against Conchita so I'm just going to have to go out and play aggressive like I did tonight," said Davenport.
